'''Don Salvador Benedicto''', officially the '''Municipality of Don Salvador Benedicto''' ({{langx|hil|Banwa sang Don Salvador Benedicto}}; {{langx|tl|Bayan ng Don Salvador Benedicto}}) or simply '''Salvador Benedicto''' and abbreviated as '''DSB''', is a [[municipality of the Philippines|municipality]] in the [[Philippine Province|province]] of [[Negros Occidental]], [[Philippines]]. According to the {{PH wikidata|population_as_of}}, it has a population of {{PH wikidata|population_total}} people.{{PH wikidata|population_reference}}

The municipality is a post-colonial provincial [[hill station]], designated the ''Summer Capital of Negros Occidental'', and is a popular tourist site.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.experiencenegros.com/things-to-see-and-do-in-don-salvador-benedicto-negros-occidental/|title=Things to see and do in Don Salvador Benedicto, Negros Occidental|publisher=Yap, Roxie|accessdate=August 24, 2008}}</ref>

==History==
{{wide image|Don Salvador Benedicto mountain range.jpg|600px|align-cap=center|Mountain ranges seen at Don Salvador Benedicto}}
The concept of establishing the municipality was initiated by Nehemias 'Nene' de la Cruz, who, while imprisoned during the [[Martial law under Ferdinand Marcos|Martial law era]], envisioned creating a town from what was considered a “cradle of insurgency.” and after his release, gained the support of his friend Mike Coronel, who was also the provincial commander of the [[Philippine Constabulary]] in [[Negros Occidental]], in establishing the upcoming municipality based in Barangay Igmaya-an, which was then part of [[Murcia, Negros Occidental|Murcia]], in 1976. Located at the center of the mountains of northern Negros Occidental, Don Salvador Benedicto was chartered in 1983 through Batas Pambansa Bilang 336 by then President [[Ferdinand Marcos]]. It consolidated all the remote barangays of [[San Carlos, Negros Occidental|San Carlos City]] and the towns of [[Calatrava, Negros Occidental|Calatrava]] and Murcia.<ref name="rappler">{{Cite news |last=Delilan |first=Erwin |date=March 28, 2024 |title=Just imagine how John Lennon's 'Imagine' inspired the creation of Negros' frontier town |work=[[Rappler]] |url=https://www.rappler.com/philippines/visayas/how-john-lennon-imagine-song-inspired-creation-don-salvador-benedicto-town-negros-occidental/ |access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref> which were apparently neglected due to inaccessibility.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}}

The town is named after the former Vice Governor Salvador Valois Benedicto (March 31, 1889–November 28, 1956) who played an important role in the setting up of a Revolutionary Government in [[Negros Island]] particularly in Barangay Igmaya-an, when the country was occupied by the Japanese during [[World War II]].<ref name="rappler"/> He was also the main guerrilla coordinator in both [[Negros Oriental]] and Negros Occidental during the said war. Salvador Benedicto is a relative of [[Roberto Benedicto]], a [[Cronies of Ferdinand Marcos|crony]] of Marcos.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}}

==Geography==
Don Salvador Benedicto is {{convert|47|km}} east of [[Bacolod]], via [[Negros Occidental Eco-Tourism Highway]] (N69) and {{convert|53|km}} from [[Calatrava, Negros Occidental|Calatrava]].

===Barangays===
Don Salvador Benedicto is politically subdivided into 7 [[barangay]]s. Each barangay consists of [[purok]]s and some have [[sitios]].
* Bago (Lalung)
* Bagong Silang (Marcelo)
* Bunga
* Igmaya-an
* Kumaliskis
* Pandanon
* Pinowayan (Prosperidad)

===Languages===
Major languages are [[Hiligaynon language|Hiligaynon]], followed by [[Cebuano language|Cebuano]]. [[Philippine English|English]] and [[Tagalog language|Tagalog]] are also understood.

==Economy==

{{PH poverty incidence}}
Although a small town, the town of Don Salvador Benedicto has seen a rise in its municipal economy thanks to tourism and local agriculture. Due to its high altitude like [[Baguio]], the town can support crops that grow in temperate areas, making it ideal for a multitude of farming businesses. Tourism is on the rise for the town especially when travellers head out into the heart of the province. Also located in the municipality are the Choco Hills, similar to Bohol's Chocolate Hills, with shared boundary of Barangay Prosperidad, [[San Carlos, Negros Occidental|San Carlos City]].<ref name="Don Salvador Benedicto Tourism">{{cite web |url=http://www.experiencenegros.com/agriculture-and-tourism-potentials-don-salvador-benedicto|title=Agriculture and Tourism Potentials of Don Salvador Benedicto|publisher=Reyes, Glady|accessdate=February 11, 2010}}</ref>
